title: Design Your Business
description: Design a complete business plan that efficiently uses all four factors of production (land, labor, capital, entrepreneurship) with realistic cost estimates, revenue projections, and viability assessment for a business that could succeed in {{STATE_NAME}}.
learning_objectives: Apply all four factors of production to design a complete business concept
Estimate realistic costs for land (rent), labor (payroll), and capital (equipment loans)
Project revenue based on pricing and sales volume assumptions
Calculate profitability and assess business viability
instructions: Brainstorm a business concept that addresses a real customer need in {{STATE_NAME}}
Name your business and select a business type (retail, food, service, tech, manufacturing, other)
Identify land requirements (location type, natural resources) and estimate monthly rent
Plan labor needs (number of employees, key roles) and estimate monthly payroll
List capital requirements (equipment, vehicles, technology) and estimate monthly loan payments
Define your entrepreneurial contribution (innovation, risk, unique value proposition)
Create revenue model with pricing and sales volume estimates
Calculate total costs, revenue, and profit to assess viability
Review feedback and viability score to refine your business plan
materials_needed: Cost estimation guides for different business types

fields.label: What problem does your business solve?
fields.prompt: Describe the customer need you're addressing
examples: Students need affordable tech repair in their neighborhood
Busy professionals want healthy grab-and-go lunch options
Homeowners need reliable lawn care without long-term contracts

fields.label: Number of employees
fields.note: 0 if you're doing all work yourself (solo entrepreneur)

fields.label: Total capital investment
fields.note: One-time purchase cost of all equipment and vehicles

fields.label: Monthly loan payment
fields.calculation_hint: Rough estimate: total investment × 0.01 for 7% loan over 5-7 years

fields.label: Your unique innovation
fields.prompt: What makes your business different from competitors?
examples: Only eco-friendly cleaning service in town

fields.label: Risk you're taking
examples: Customer demand might be lower than expected

fields.label: Target monthly profit
fields.note: Your goal as entrepreneur - what you want to earn after all costs

fields.label: Average price
fields.note: Average selling price per item or service

fields.label: Monthly sales volume
fields.note: How many units or services you expect to sell each month

90_to_100.message: Outstanding business plan with strong profit potential!

75_to_89.message: Solid business plan with reasonable profit margins.

60_to_74.message: Viable business but margins are tight. Look for ways to improve.

below_60.message: Business plan needs refinement to improve profitability.

profitability_feedback.loss: ⚠️ Your business would operate at a loss. Increase prices, volume, or reduce costs.
profitability_feedback.break_even: ⚡ Profit is minimal. Consider if the risk is worth this return.
profitability_feedback.low_profit: 💡 Profit is positive but could be higher. Look for efficiency improvements.
profitability_feedback.good_profit: ✅ Profitable business model! Good factor allocation.

labor_feedback.no_payroll: 💡 No payroll? Are you doing all the work yourself (your labor)?
labor_feedback.high_labor_ratio: 👥 Labor is your biggest cost. Consider automation or efficiency improvements.

capital_feedback.no_capital: 💡 No capital costs? Make sure you've accounted for equipment loans or depreciation.
capital_feedback.high_capital: 🏭 Significant capital investment. Ensure revenue justifies equipment costs.

pricing_feedback.low_price_high_volume: 📊 Low price, high volume strategy. Make sure you can deliver at scale.
pricing_feedback.high_price_low_volume: 💎 Premium pricing strategy. Ensure customers see value at this price point.
pricing_feedback.balanced: ⚖️ Balanced pricing and volume. Test these assumptions with market research.

deliverables: Complete business concept with clear value proposition
Detailed factor requirements for land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship
Revenue model with pricing and volume projections
Financial analysis showing costs, revenue, profit, and viability score
Feedback on business plan strengths and areas for improvement

group_config.optional_pair_work: Students may work in pairs to brainstorm but should complete own business plan

criteria: Identified realistic requirements for all four factors of production
Created revenue model with reasonable price and volume assumptions
Calculated profitability accurately with proper cost and revenue estimates
Demonstrated understanding of entrepreneurial risk and innovation
Developed viable business concept that could succeed in real market

teacher_notes: This culminating activity synthesizes the entire chapter. Students apply all four factors to design their own business, making economics tangible and personal. Encourage creativity but demand realism - costs and revenues should be researched or estimated based on actual data. Many students will design unprofitable businesses initially; this is a valuable learning experience about why entrepreneurship is risky and why careful planning matters. The viability scoring provides objective feedback. Extension: Have students pitch their businesses to the class (30 seconds each) and vote on most viable concepts. This activity often sparks genuine entrepreneurial interest - some students may actually pursue these ideas!
